accepted.question_text: Let C be a hereditary class of graphs. Suppose there exists a polynomial-time algorithm that computes the stable set number of every graph G in C. Must C then be χ-bounded, meaning that there exists a function f such that every graph G in C satisfies χ(G) ≤ f(ω(G)), where χ(G) is the chromatic number and ω(G) is the clique number?

evidence.quote:
Nicolas Trotignon: We will use the following deﬁnition:
Deﬁnition. A hereditary class of graphs is χ-bounded if there exists a function f such
that for every graph G in the class: χ(G)≤f(ω(G)).
Suppose that there exists a polynomial time algorithm to compute the stable set number
for all graphs in a class C. Then is C χ-bounded?

accepted.question_text: A graph G = (V, E) is called k-thin if there exist an ordering < of the vertices of G and a partition of V into k sets such that, for every triple of vertices r < s < t, if r and s lie in the same part and {t, r} is an edge, then {t, s} is also an edge. Is there a characterization of the 2-thin graphs?

evidence.quote:
Flavia Bonomo: We will use the following deﬁnition:
Deﬁnition. A graph G = (V,E ) is k-thin if there exist an ordering < of the vertices of G
and a partition of V into k sets with the property that, for each triple of vertices r,s,t with
r<s<t , if r and s are in the same partitioned set and {t,r} is an edge, then {t,s} is an
edge.
Is there a characterization for the 2-thin graphs?
